Ask yourself: why would a language model that relies on pretraining data need retrieval at all? For example, if a user asks about recent, widely discussed news, what can't the model do on its own, and how does RAG fill that gap?","citationIds":["c1"]},{"text":"Next, think about when retrieval is needed. Is retrieval useful for every instruction? Consider \"Give three tips for staying healthy\" versus \"Describe a time when you had to make a difficult decision.\" What differs between them, and why might one benefit from external documents while the other doesn't?","citationIds":["c2"]},{"text":"Push the boundary further. Why might a math question like finding a circle's area from its radius not need retrieval, even though documents with the formula exist? And why might even a well-known fact like the capital of France still benefit from retrieval?","citationIds":["c3"]},{"text":"Now consider the query itself. If a user's query is ambiguous, too brief, or reflects uncertainty about what they want, what could you do to the query before retrieving? How might adding meaningful terms (query expansion) help? And for a complex request with several parts, what might decomposing it into sub-queries achieve?","citationIds":["c4"]},{"text":"Finally, think about optimizing and evaluating retrieval. Which parts of the retrieval pipeline could you improve (indexing, query, embedding)? When comparing methods such as BM25, Contriever, GTR, and ColBERTv2 against multi-step approaches, what would recall@2 versus recall@5 tell you? And when might single-step retrieval be insufficient, so that multi-step retrieval becomes worthwhile?","citationIds":["c1","c5"]}],"citations":[{"id":"c1","chunkId":"396a0fadeb4cd40f_c_589bc4e8cae01e02","docId":"396a0fadeb4cd40f","docTitle":"2312.10997_Retrieval_Augmented_Generation_for_Large_Language_Models_A_Survey","page":2,"quote":"Here, a user poses a question to ChatGPT about a recent, widely discussed news."},{"id":"c2","chunkId":"d9eaa1398abac0df_c_9f9f8e3c98bd1183","docId":"d9eaa1398abac0df","docTitle":"2310.11511_Self_RAG_Learning_to_Retrieve_Generate_and_Critique_through_Self_Refle","page":25,"quote":"There might be some online sources listing three tips for staying healthy or some reliable sources to explain the effects of different behaviors on health."},{"id":"c3","chunkId":"d9eaa1398abac0df_c_248ad29a10e559a1","docId":"d9eaa1398abac0df","docTitle":"2310.11511_Self_RAG_Learning_to_Retrieve_Generate_and_Critique_through_Self_Refle","page":26,"quote":"This is a math question and although we may be able to find some documents describing a formula, it is unlikely to find a document exactly mentioning the answer."},{"id":"c4","chunkId":"737b0b8fe0aa8459_c_5a8a1f096ee2ab5e","docId":"737b0b8fe0aa8459","docTitle":"2501.00309_Retrieval_Augmented_Generation_with_Graphs_GraphRAG","page":8,"quote":"Query Expansion enriches a query by adding meaningful terms with similar significance [12], which primarily addresses three challenges: (1) user-submitted queries are ambiguous and relate to multiple topics; (2) queries may be too brief to"},{"id":"c5","chunkId":"14671c78fc7de99d_c_1561f63effe8dae8","docId":"14671c78fc7de99d","docTitle":"2405.14831_HippoRAG_Neurobiologically_Inspired_Long_Term_Memory_for_Large_Languag","page":5,"quote":"We compare against several strong and widely used retrieval methods: BM25 [69], Contriever [35], GTR [53] and ColBERTv2 [70]."}]}}}
